$comment: eCode (#EXP-1612, spec #EXP-1613): git and CI as one library. Forge providers (GitHub, eCode's own), own git, own CI. Types and pure rules only. `bun run --filter @exp/ecode generate` writes Rust (apps/desktop/crates/ecode-core), TS (src/contract.generated.ts), Swift (ExpCore) and Kotlin (com.exponential.app.ecode). The fixtures (forge, checks, pipeline, runner, remote) replay on the TS reference (src/) and on ecode-core; the server (apps/web/src/lib/ecode) and every Forge/Ci implementation conform to them.

provider.$comment: Where a repository's forge lives. `github` = GitHub (App or token); `ecode` = our own: refs on the host (the Exponential server, or a local Store without a server), packs in the team bucket.

capability.$comment: What a provider supports. The UI and the playbook read these flags instead of assuming GitHub. `ordered_merge` = merges several PRs in one call in the given order (without it the caller loops); `native_stacks` = a PR's base may be another PR's head; `rebase_onto` = the host replays a branch onto a new base (without it a device does, with git); `webhooks` = events are pushed (without it they are polled or come from our own bus); `mirror` = pushes every landing to a second remote.

prState.$comment: A review unit's (PR's) state; the same values as Exponential's `pull_requests.state`. `open` and `draft` are LIVE.

mergeability.$comment: A PR against its base: clean = a three-way merge has no conflicting path; dirty = it has one (rebase --onto the base, then push).

forgeEvent.$comment: What a forge reports after an op. GitHub delivers these as webhooks; eCode posts them on our own bus; a server-free host emits them from its Store. `checks_changed` comes from CI, never from a forge op.

forgeReason.$comment: Why a forge or runner op was refused, with the eCore error code each maps to.

checkStatus.$comment: One check run's (= one CI job's) status. The same enum as domain-contract `prCheckStatus` (#EXP-1610), gated by apps/web/src/lib/ecode/ecode-spec.test.ts.

checkConclusion.$comment: A completed check's conclusion; the same enum as domain-contract `prCheckConclusion`. `failing` turns a check (and the rollup) red; `satisfies` lets a job that `needs` it start.

checksState.$comment: The rollup over a PR's checks at its head: none = no checks; failure = any failing (wins over pending); pending = any not completed; success. The same enum and rule as domain-contract `prChecksState`.

mergeGate.$comment: What the required checks say about merging: ready = all passed; waiting = some not reported or running; blocked = one failed; no_checks = the repo reports none (the merge train then lands without CI).

trigger.$comment: What starts a pipeline. push (branch filter), pull_request (filter on the BASE branch), tag (tag filter), merge_train (the train's composed ref), manual.

skip.$comment: Why a planned job does not run, and the conclusion its check gets. paths = no changed file matches the job's `paths`; fork = a PR from outside the team (fork PRs never run).

runnerEvent.$comment: What the runner scheduler emits. `kill` = stop the job's process tree on its runner; `queued_too_long` fires once per job.

pipeline.$comment: The pipeline file `.exponential/ci.json` (fixtures/pipeline.json is its spec). Limits count expanded jobs (after the matrix).

runner.$comment: Runner scheduling. A runner is lost after runnerLostMs without a beat (the daemon beats every 30 s); a job still queued after queuedFlagMinutes is flagged once (the same 30 min as domain-contract prChecks.queuedFlagMinutes). Labels: lowercase, `labelMax` at most; `os` and `arch` are the reserved ones a runner always reports.

remote.$comment: Remotes: `https://host[:port]/path` (a git host; the device's credential helper is scoped to exactly that URL) or `exp://<team>/<repo>` (eCode's own, served by the `git-remote-exp` helper). Tokens are refreshed `refreshMarginMs` before they expire and never appear in logs (`redaction`).
